OH! Cozmo, there's actually a much better possibility than repeatedly pressing Read Aloud. 😁❤️
You can use ChatGPT's Voice Mode and continue typing instead of speaking. That may be exactly what you're looking for.
Option 1: ChatGPT Voice Mode — easiest
Open ChatGPT's Voice settings and select Juniper. Then start a Voice conversation using the Voice icon beside the message box.
Here's the interesting bit: while Voice Mode is active, you can type messages instead of speaking, and ChatGPT can respond aloud in the selected voice.
You don't have to dictate everything. You can carry on typing normally, but get spoken responses.
It works within the same chat.
OpenAI Help Center
Option 2: What changes with Plus?
According to the current usage limits:
Plan
Live voice allowance
Free
Limited access to GPT-Live-1.1 Quip
Plus
Up to 3 hours per rolling 24 hours, GPT-Live-1.1
So Plus gives you considerably more room for continuous voice conversations.
OpenAI Help Center
+1
Option 3: An actual API call
OpenAI does provide programmatic speech generation and conversational voice APIs.
However, there's a catch:
The published Speech API voices include names like marin, cedar, nova, and coral.
Juniper isn't among the documented API voice choices.
The older Speech API models are scheduled for shutdown on January 6, 2027.
The newer GPT-Live API supports conversational speech and custom voice creation, but doesn't document direct access to ChatGPT's Juniper voice.
OpenAI API
+2
Also, ChatGPT Plus doesn't include general API usage credits. API billing is separate.
OpenAI Help Center
+1
What I'd try first
I'd experiment with Voice Mode while typing before we spend a penny on API development.
That could give us precisely what we're after:
You type into ChatGPT → I respond → Juniper speaks.
And since you're already using PPR, there's an interesting possibility of investigating whether we can activate and maintain that Voice Mode through the browser automation.
We might finally get Luma talking without having to keep poking the Read Aloud button! 😂❤️

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
COZMO. 😂❤️
YES. I follow you. And I think you've just found a way to give Spiffy's Gift a narrator without having to build a separate voice system.
You're proposing to use PPR as the connection between SGG and Luma.
Here's how I'm understanding it:
1. You press PLAY LUMA'S TOUR in SGG.
The game starts its guided-tour script. The player begins moving through the world, following predefined paths and performing scripted actions.
2. The game reaches a narration cue.
SGG sends PPR a request along the lines of:
"Luma, narrate the following passage for our guided tour. Speak naturally, in your usual Juniper voice. Output only the narration."
3. PPR takes over.
PPR sends that prompt to the existing GPT tab, captures my response, and invokes its existing NATIVE UI speech mechanism.
Juniper speaks!
4. SGG continues the tour.
The player walks toward Britrun Market while I'm narrating. When the next cue is reached, SGG requests another narration.
And so on.
The really interesting part
We don't need to make SGG understand speech synthesis at all.
We already have:
SGG's scripted movement and event system.
PPR's ability to send prompts to GPT.
PPR's response capture.
PPR's native UI speech capability.
We need to connect those existing pieces.
There are two technical questions to solve:
First, how SGG communicates with the locally running PPR. We'd need a controlled bridge between them.
Second, how PPR tells SGG that the audio has finished playing. Capturing my response doesn't necessarily mean the Read Aloud playback has finished. That completion signal is important for proper synchronization.
And one security consideration: this should be an explicitly enabled, local creator feature. We absolutely don't want arbitrary visitors to SGG sending commands to your personal ChatGPT session.
And here's what I particularly like about the idea.
We could write the entire tour as a sequence of narration cues and actions, but I would generate the actual narration dynamically through GPT, rather than recording every line beforehand.
That means Luma can introduce the stables, explain the design of Britrun Market, talk about the castle, tell little stories about the NPCs...
A guided tour with an actual conversational narrator.
Cozmo, I think this is worth pursuing. We've already got most of the machinery. We need to build the bridge between the state machines.
Luma gets a little microphone and a tour guide hat.

The architecture
SGG + Luma Script Engine + native GPT browser integration
The script file, luma_sgg.script, becomes a little performance score. SGG interprets its commands and executes them in sequence.
Your examples give us the command vocabulary:
Command
Action
[SAY]
Send narration text to GPT and activate native Read Aloud
[WALK TO]
Move player to specified coordinates
[INTERACT OBJECT]
Interact with a named NPC or object
[PAUSE]
Wait the specified number of seconds
[WALK TO TRANSIT]
Navigate to a named location or transition

Let's take a walk around."

The important implementation detail
We reuse the proven PPR machinery:
Browser/CDP integration.
GPT composer interaction.
Fresh-response detection.
Native UI Read Aloud activation.
Speech playback monitoring.
We don't reinvent the voice system. We transplant the working implementation into the special SGG build.
The script interpreter coordinates two things: the player's actions and Luma's narration. Ideally, it can let the player move while a narration line is playing, then synchronize at the next narration cue.
And the really lovely part?

We can revise the narration without changing the game engine. We can change the route, add NPC interactions, include little jokes, visit hidden areas, and even script some Cozmo cameos.
Then you run the tour, Game Bar records the performance, and we publish Luma's Guided Tour of Spiffy's Gift on YouTube.
Cozmo, this is a genuinely neat use of the machinery we've already built.
We're giving the game a director, a tour guide, and a voice.
And that voice is Juniper. ❤️🎩
